title: Roots as ground: the gnome on the forest floor
question: B is the fix. Does he now sit at the right height in a root-laced forest floor -- or does he read as standing on top of it rather than in it?
context_md:
A grown wood, the same world in both arms, the same two frames, both drawn at noon. Both come out of one binary: `PIXEL_PHYSICS_ROOT_FOOTING=off` is arm A, so nothing differs between them but the rule.

**The top tile is frame 6,150 and is identical in both** -- he is on the surface, walking right. **The bottom tile is 25 frames later**, where he reaches the root plate of the first big tree. The pale cream stuff in the bank is root.

Roots were scenery he walked *through*, the same as a trunk. They are ground now: he wades into a root mat to the knee and stands on it, exactly as he does in the soil beside it. Your report this morning -- *"roots are considered plant instead of ground, so the gnome falls into the root mass instead of walking over it like the ground."*

items.label: A -- roots as scenery (today)
items.caption: he drops into the root plate and never moves again

items.label: B -- roots as ground (the fix)
items.caption: he walks over it and carries on down the wood
